decision: Adopt the conv-as-streaming fixed-kernel transport of loliverhennigh/Lattice-Boltzmann-fluid-flow-in-Tensorflow as a TensorLBM transport option (`tensorlbm.streaming_conv`)? Decide by (a) implementation equivalence against the in-house gather transport and (b) physical accuracy of the transported solution against the closed-form Taylor-Green solution and the closed-form Poiseuille profile.

alternatives.A_native_gather: tensorlbm.solver.stream -- advanced-index gather over shifted source cells, per-direction indices cached; the current production transport.
alternatives.B_conv_fixed_kernel: conv-as-streaming: one fixed 3x3 depthwise cross-correlation kernel (tap index = 1 - c_axis) over circular-padded fields; wall bounce as a 1x1 cross-channel convolution blended through the solid mask (upstream LatFlow/Domain.py::StreamSC + CollideSC).
alternatives.REF_analytic: closed-form 2D Taylor-Green (exact Navier-Stokes) for the periodic arm and closed-form plane Poiseuille (Hagen-Poiseuille) parabola for the wall arm -- no interpolation, no series truncation.

hypothesis: H1: replacing only the transport operator (A -> B) leaves the solution unchanged to round-off (< 1e-12 relative max velocity) and keeps the Taylor-Green decay rate and the Poiseuille profile within 3% of the closed forms (owner gate: 15%). H0 (falsifier): any predeclared KPI deviates by >= 15%, or the transport reformulation is not equivalent to round-off.

metrics.gamma_K_rel_err_pct: kinetic-energy decay rate from a least-squares fit of ln K(t) over the second half of the run, compared with 4*nu*k^2 (percent)
metrics.field_l2_pct: ||u_num - u_exact||_2 / ||u_exact||_2 over all nodes at the final step (percent)
metrics.pair_max_rel: max|u_A - u_B| / max|u_A| over all nodes at the final step (dimensionless)
metrics.u_center_rel_err_pct: steady channel centreline velocity vs g*H^2/(8*nu) with the nominal half-way wall spacing H = Ny-2 (percent)

unit_of_analysis: one transport arm at one (resolution, Reynolds) configuration; every KPI is a scalar per arm-configuration

baseline_control.baseline: arm A at the reference configuration (n=128, Re=100, U0=0.05)
baseline_control.control: arm B at the identical configuration: the single changed variable is the transport operator; collision (BGK), initial condition, sampling, dtype and thread count are shared code paths
baseline_control.reference: closed-form Taylor-Green and Hagen-Poiseuille (not another solver), so the accuracy statement is independent of any implementation choice

predeclared_thresholds.exactness_note: the fixed kernel has exactly one unit tap per output channel, so a faithful port is expected to be bit-wise identical to the gather transport; the 1e-12 band is a tolerance, not a target
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is resolution-converged when |KPI(n=128) - KPI(n=64)| / |KPI(n=128)| < 10%
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run whose population contains a non-finite value, or whose |u| exceeds 10*U0, is declared failed and reported, not re-tuned

sensitivity_points: resolution n in {64, 128} at Re=100, U0=0.05 (discretisation)
Reynolds number Re in {50, 100} at n=128, U0=0.05 (tau = 0.885 vs 0.692, i.e. the less-damped regime)
channel height Ny in {16, 32} for the wall arm (bounce formulation)
stopping_rule: fixed step counts chosen before the run from the analytic decay/viscous time scale (TG: 4900 steps = 2.9 e-folding times of K at Re=100; channel: 30000 steps = 3.3 viscous times H^2/nu). No arm is extended or truncated after inspecting a KPI.
variables_controlled: initial condition f = f_eq(rho, u0) on cell centres x_i = i + 0.5
float64 CPU torch, fixed thread count
confounders: upstream is TensorFlow 1.x float32 on GPU; the transplant is torch float64 on CPU -- the comparison is formulation-level, not bit-level against upstream's binaries

upstream's D3Q19 STREAM table contains one wrong tap (q=3); the port therefore derives kernels from the velocity table and only re-uses upstream's D2Q9 table (verified consistent), so the D3Q19 path is NOT cross-validated against upstream's shipped numbers
the Poiseuille arm needs a body force; both arms share one Guo forcing implementation, so forcing error is common-mode and not attributed to the transport operator
repetition_rationale: both arms are deterministic (zero variance), so repetition is replaced by (a) two independent physical cases (periodic + wall), (b) three predeclared sensitivity configurations, (c) three independent equivalence checks (2D bitwise, 3D vs canonical roll traversal, upstream-table audit).

environment.solver: TensorLBM src/tensorlbm (torch 2.7.1, CPU only -- torch.cuda.is_available() == False)

analysis_plan: table arm x configuration with every KPI and its percent deviation from the closed form; verdict by the predeclared 15% rule with the 3% internal target reported separately; uncertainty = resolution delta + Re delta; no post-hoc threshold change.
sections_delivered: reference vs got table with pass/fail marks
difference list: TensorLBM vs upstream (method / parameters / boundary conditions) + porting trade-offs
